lines.text: Do you know how a compass finds north? The needle isn't pointing at a place. It's lining up with the whole planet.
Deep inside the Earth, molten iron swirls around the core. That moving metal makes the planet into a giant magnet.
Invisible magnetic field lines loop out of one end of the Earth, and back into the other.
A compass needle is a tiny magnet, balanced so it can spin freely. It swings until it lines up with those field lines.
Here's the twist. The magnetic north pole isn't the same as the true North Pole. It's hundreds of kilometres away, and it wanders every year.
Chinese inventors were using magnetic compasses about a thousand years ago, and they changed sea travel forever.
So every compass is a tiny magnet, holding hands with the planet.
